data.Branch: U.S. Air Force (Joint Base San Antonio)
data.Mission: Air Force & Space Force Basic Military Training (BMT)

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: JBSA-Lackland is home to the 37th Training Wing, the largest training wing in the U.S. Air Force and known as the 'Gateway to the Air Force.'

Its 737th Training Group runs Basic Military Training (BMT), the Department of the Air Force's only enlisted basic training location, for more than 36,000 Air Force and Space Force recruits a year, alongside a wide range of technical and professional training. Installation support across all of JBSA comes from the 502d Air Base Wing, and JBSA is the Department of Defense's largest joint base.

source.label: 37th Training Wing fact sheet; 737th Training Group (official)

data.subtitle: Lackland is the only Basic Military Training site for the Air Force and Space Force, so for most families the reason you're here is graduation week.
intro: Graduation week is when you'll see your Airman or Guardian for the first time since they shipped out. Families travel to San Antonio from across the country for it, and a little planning makes the trip far less stressful.

Graduation week centers on two mornings: the Airman's Run (7:30 a.m.) and the Coin Ceremony (9:30 a.m.) on Wednesday at the Pfingston Reception Center, and the graduation parade at 9 a.m. on Thursday. Schedules, locations, dress expectations, and base-access rules can change, so always confirm the current details on the official BMT graduation site before you travel.

recommendations.advice: Each trainee can invite six guests aged 18 or older; children under 18 don't need a separate pass. Adult guests need a REAL ID-compliant ID (or an alternative such as a passport) with their guest pass. The Air Force sends guests who drive to the Selfridge West or Valley Hi gate; on Thursday Selfridge West is open only until 8 a.m., so later arrivals should use Valley Hi, which is open 24 hours. Plan ahead for traffic at the Lackland gates.
Graduation weeks fill up fast. On-base lodging is limited, but there are plenty of hotels near the base and across San Antonio.

recommendations.who: Make a long weekend of it
recommendations.advice: Most families do. The River Walk, the Alamo, and San Antonio's food scene are all close by.

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Four gates are open 24 hours: Luke East, Valley Hi, McMullen and the Chapman Training Annex gate. Selfridge West, Selfridge East, Tinker and Security Hill keep weekday or part-day hours, the Growdon commercial gate runs 5 a.m. to 5 p.m. (closed on federal holidays), and Luke West is closed.

Visitors without a DoD ID enter through a visitor center. The Luke East Visitor Center (Bldg. 1196, 2602 Luke Blvd, 210-671-6174) reopened around the clock on October 16, 2026; the Valley Hi and McMullen visitor centers are closed. Hours change, so confirm on the official gate page before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-base family housing is Lackland Family Homes, owned and run by Balfour Beatty Communities, in six neighborhoods set by rank: Airman Scott Village, Frank Tejeda East and West and North Wherry for E-1 to E-6, North Skeet for E-7 to E-9 and O-1 to O-6, and Lemay Estates for O-6 to O-9. Frank Tejeda West is also open to retirees, DoD civilians and the public.

The Air Force Housing page says homes aren't metered and rent covers utilities up to your full BAH; confirm with the operator. No wait times are posted, so contact the Military Housing Office (2525 Fairchild St, Bldg. 1524, (210) 671-1840) or the Lackland Family Homes leasing office ((210) 674-9366).

source.label: DoD BAH Rate Lookup (MHA TX285, CY2026)

sections.title: Schools
data: On base, schooling is the civilian Lackland Independent School District: Lackland Elementary (pre-K to 5) and Virginia Allred Stacey Jr/Sr High School (6 to 12). It earned a B (87) in Texas's 2026 ratings, with a 100% graduation rate for the class of 2025. There is no DoDEA district here.

Children living on base attend automatically. Lackland ISD also takes a limited number of off-base transfer students each year, first come, first served, from families of active-duty members assigned to JBSA, military retirees, and JBSA or district civilians, after current transfer students who renew on time.

Off base, the district depends on the address. Districts on the west and southwest side include Northside ISD (C, 78 in 2026), Southwest ISD (B, 80) and Medina Valley ISD (B, 82), and campus ratings vary within a district, so confirm the district and campus for any address. School Liaison: 210-671-8388, jbsa.slo@us.af.mil.

data.Care: Outpatient, ambulatory surgery and urgent care (listed as 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily)
data.Emergency room: None on base since April 4, 2026; Brooke Army Medical Center at Fort Sam Houston is the primary military ER

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the local market, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at the local military treatment facility or network providers.

data.q: Why am I coming to Lackland?
data.a: Lackland runs Air Force and Space Force Basic Military Training, so for many families the visit is graduation week. It is also home to the 37th Training Wing and a great deal of technical training.

data.q: How do I attend a BMT graduation?
data.a: Graduation events run on Wednesday and Thursday: the Airman's Run and Coin Ceremony on Wednesday morning and the parade at 9 a.m. on Thursday. Each trainee can invite six guests aged 18 or older, who need a REAL ID (or an alternative such as a passport) with their guest pass. Check the official BMT graduation site for the current schedule and rules before you travel.

data.q: On base or off base in San Antonio?
data.a: On-base family housing is Lackland Family Homes, run by Balfour Beatty Communities, in six neighborhoods set by rank. Off base, the school district changes from one address to the next, so confirm the district and campus before you sign.
All of the JBSA bases share MHA TX285 (San Antonio). Use the calculator above for your grade.
